Class ExtraCredentialAuthorizationResolver

java.lang.Object
org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.security.ExtraCredentialAuthorizationResolver
All Implemented Interfaces:
AuthorizationResolver
public final class ExtraCredentialAuthorizationResolver extends Object implements AuthorizationResolver
AuthorizationResolver that reads a session's authorization tokens from a Trino extra credential carrying a base64url-encoded token list. The decoded payload is a comma or whitespace delimited list. Base64url keeps the wire value free of the extraCredentials pair delimiters by construction. Intended for deployments fronted by a trusted service mesh that authenticates the caller and injects the authoritative token set: the mesh base64url-encodes its identity header (e.g. x-auths) into Trino's X-Trino-Extra-Credential client header, which Trino exposes here via ConnectorIdentity.getExtraCredentials().

Because the tokens flow through unchanged there is no mapping file to maintain and nothing to drift from the platform's clearances. Selected with: 

  geomesa.security.auth-resolver=org.locationtech.geomesa.trino.security.ExtraCredentialAuthorizationResolver
  geomesa.security.auths-credential=auths   # optional; the extra-credential name (default "auths")

A missing or empty credential resolves to an empty set — fail-closed (the row filter then admits only unrestricted rows). This trusts the extra credential implicitly, so the deployment MUST ensure only trusted callers can set it. When the transport can't be locked down to the trusted caller (e.g. no mesh AuthorizationPolicy), configure a shared secret via geomesa.security.auths-secret: the caller must then also present a matching secret extra credential or NO auths are honored. The secret value must not contain a comma or colon (the Trino extraCredentials wire format uses name:value,name:value); generate it hex/base64url.
